result.model: Linear moving-exterior response with one straight channel and prescribed displacement

equations.displacement: h(s)=a*D*256*z^4*(1-z)^4 for z=s/T in (0,1), zero outside; h is C3 and already includes a.
equations.motion_source: i=(h third derivative+Omega squared*h first derivative)/3. For each k>=0 the A drive uses x-kL-pi/2-D and B uses x-kL-pi/2.
equations.recurrence: j_A-j_A(x-L)=c0*Q[A+A_L-B_D-B_pi]+i_A, with A/B interchanged for j_B; P A=-j_A and P B=-j_B, no injected carrier.
equations.clocks: xi_A(s)=[integral A(s+pi/2)-integral B(s-pi/2)]/b0; xi_B exchanges A and B. Rates are 1+xi prime.
equations.returns: C_A=L+xi_A(s)-xi_B(s+pi)+h(s+pi); C_B=L+xi_B(s)-xi_A(s+pi)+h(s+pi+D), only to first order.
equations.outgoing: delta qout_i(s)=j_other(s-pi/2)+2Q0*xi_i prime-xi_i third derivative/3; Q0=-Omega squared/6.
equations.reduced_ledger: B=-b0*sum(xi third derivative+xi prime); E0=integral from s-D to s of sum(delta qout). B+E0=[h second derivative(s)+h second derivative(s-D)+Omega squared*(h(s)+h(s-D))]/3.

result.scope: Retarded finite-time, first-order leading-JT/CFT calculation with one externally prescribed straight-channel displacement. Background frequencies and induced histories use unshifted times; shifting an already first-order history would add second-order terms. Clock and return extrema are sampled; times are linearized, not exact finite-amplitude transit. Direct geometric and induced-clock return changes are separately recorded; T=4 allows early nonnegative launches to sample the moving exterior at exit. The reduced ledger omits moving-domain vacuum energy (including 2Q0*h), geometric terms and higher-order production. Its effective drive is not mechanical work, a full4D energy budget or net particle production. No physical mouth matching, preparation, nonlinear stability, apparatus or human passage is demonstrated.
result.independent_validation: moving_exterior_maps.py separately tests the exact moving-endpoint null maps, covariant stress transformation and amplitude-halving limit; this helper tests their coupled linear recurrence.
